gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Amazfit's HYROX sensor, the $199.99 Helio Strap Pro, works only with the Balance 3 and Balance Ultra, so none of the sub-$150 HYROX-mode watches (Bip 6, Active 2) can use its HYROX Race/Simulation analysis. Amazfit's tested list of devices that can receive the $99.99 Helio Strap's heart-rate broadcast names no Amazfit watch, though it does name the COROS Pace 3 and Garmin Forerunner 165.
standout_why: Compared against dealectric.com (ours), roxskin.io and the5krunner. Our page doesn't cover strap or external-HR compatibility at all. Roxskin.io says only that the Helio Strap Pro 'needs a compatible Amazfit watch' without naming which, and it marks the Active 2 as chest-strap capable with no strap named or sourced. The cited rivals (us.amazfit.com Active 2 page, coros.com, tomsguide, techradar, bestbuy) are product pages or general running-watch roundups, and none gives a watch-by-accessory pairing. The other HYROX results (hyroxvegas, roxgrit, hyroxinsider, protocolathletes, wearablebeat) were not opened. In one chat ChatGPT told the shopper to 'save the remaining $50 for a heart-rate chest strap', and no result tells them which strap works with which watch.
decides: This supports the Bip 6 / Active 2 as the under-$150 pick for the race mode itself. It also stops a wrong add-on purchase: Amazfit's own HYROX strap does not unlock HYROX analysis on either cheap watch, because that needs a Balance 3 ($369.99) or Balance Ultra. Amazfit doesn't list either cheap watch as a confirmed receiver for the $99.99 Helio Strap. The page should send strap buyers to a standard Bluetooth HR strap, and only after confirming support on Amazfit's peripherals list, which I couldn't open. Small extra: Amazfit's $24.99 HYROX-branded strap is 22 mm, so it fits the Bip 6 but not the Active 2, which uses 20 mm bands.
